# Closed-Loop Null-Space Exploration

## Status

Evidence class: specification only, not approved. This chapter records the
mathematical specification delivered by NSX-00 (#12549) for epic #12593 so the
pathway can be inventoried. No calculation is registered. The registry blocker
`UP-NSX-loop-nullspace-exploration` stays open until the implementing children
land, UP-D1 inventories the pathway and a human reviews it.

The standalone research reference is
`docs/research/loop_nullspace/loop_nullspace.tex`. It is editable separately
from this manual and is not a manual artifact.

## Purpose

Describe every torque and hand-load family that is consistent with one
measured two-handed swing, and report which quantities are the same for the
whole family. The motion fixes the generalized load and the net bare-club
wrench. It does not fix how that load divides between the hands or between
joints inside the loop.

## Conventions

- Unknowns $x = (\tau, \lambda, f_g)$ and the allocation equation
  $$A x = b, \qquad A = \begin{bmatrix} S^{\top} & J_c^{\top} & J_g^{\top}
  \end{bmatrix}, \qquad b = M(q)\,a + h(q, v).$$
- Closure rows are $[f_x\ f_y\ f_z\ \tau_x\ \tau_y\ \tau_z]$ in the grip
  frame. The term $+J_c^{\top}\lambda$ acts on the human tree, so the closing
  hand exerts $-\lambda$ on the club.
- Hand wrenches follow the ADR-0052 sign: loading exerted by the hand on the
  club.

## Equations

1. Rank accounting. With $u$ the unactuated rows:
   $$\operatorname{rank} A = n_a + \operatorname{rank}\begin{bmatrix}
   J_{c,u}^{\top} & J_{g,u}^{\top}\end{bmatrix}$$
   $$\text{nullity} = m + n_g - \operatorname{rank}\begin{bmatrix}
   J_{c,u}^{\top} & J_{g,u}^{\top}\end{bmatrix}$$
2. Multiplier gauge $m - \operatorname{rank} J_c$. Attainable torque variation
   $\operatorname{rank} J_c^{\top} - \operatorname{rank} J_{c,u}^{\top}$ when
   $f_g$ is fixed.
3. Zero-side residual for a side with transposed Jacobian $J_s^{\top}$:
   $$\left\lVert \left(I - J_s^{\top}(J_s^{\top})^{+}\right)\tau_{ID,s}
   \right\rVert$$
4. Grasp map $G\in\mathbb{R}^{6\times 12}$ and kernel $K\in\mathbb{R}^{12\times 6}$
   with $G K = 0$; the split coordinates are $s = \Phi\, y$.

The full derivations, goldens and worked examples are in the research
reference and in `tests/fixtures/loop_nullspace/goldens`.

## Variability Sensitivity

Evidence class: software specification of a first-order model, not approved.
Phase 8 (NSX-80 to NSX-100) asks how much the face angle at impact varies under
declared disturbances and which strategies change that. The contract text is
`docs/research/loop_nullspace/contracts_variability.md`; the derivations are in
the standalone reference `docs/research/loop_nullspace/loop_nullspace.tex`
(section `sec:variability`). No number below describes a real golfer.

### Model and Equations

1. Linearization. On the tangent bundle of the closed-loop manifold, with the
   reactions re-solved, the state error $\delta x_t$ evolves as
   $$\delta x_{t+1} = A_t\,\delta x_t + B_t\,w_t, \qquad
   w_t \sim (0, \Sigma_t),$$
   where $w_t$ is the declared disturbance, $\Sigma_t$ its covariance from the
   disturbance specification (a spectral density, with the time step
   declared), and $A_t$, $B_t$ the derivatives of the constrained solve.
2. Covariance recursion.
   $$P_{t+1} = A_t P_t A_t^{\top} + B_t \Sigma_t B_t^{\top}.$$
3. Outcome variance. For an outcome row $C$ (the face-angle row of the impact
   outcome map, or $C\,\Pi$ across an impact event with saltation matrix $S$),
   $$\operatorname{Var}(y) = C P_T C^{\top}.$$
   The adjoint form gives the same value through kernels $S_{y,x_0}$ and
   $S_{y,\tau}(t)$ and splits it by input class and by step. The parts sum to
   the total; shares are unavailable when the total is not positive.
4. Mechanisms. M1 signal-dependent noise, M2 geometric preload and M3 muscle
   impedance are declared one at a time. With none declared and additive noise,
   the objective gradient is zero and every allocation is equivalent; the
   result is flagged objective-flat rather than ranked.
5. Face angle. The error is wrapped to $(-\pi, \pi]$. Reported outcomes are
   bias, standard deviation, interquartile range, exceedance and miss
   probability. A coefficient of variation is not used for a zero-centred
   outcome.
6. Strategy comparison. Each arm is a strategy at a declared setting. Arms are
   ordered by the ratio of their face-angle variance to the strategy-off
   baseline of their own model representation. An arm whose ratio is not below
   one cannot win. Arms outside the matched-speed or matched-effort limits are
   excluded, not relaxed.
7. Structure of real variability (NSX-97). For swing states $x_i$ and the
   outcome Jacobian $C$, the variance in $\ker C$ (UCM) and in its orthogonal
   complement (ORT) are divided by their dimensions, with
   $$\Delta V = \frac{V_{\mathrm{UCM}}/d_{\mathrm{UCM}} - V_{\mathrm{ORT}}/d_{\mathrm{ORT}}}
   {V_{\mathrm{TOT}}/n}.$$
   The tolerance-noise-covariation decomposition uses permutation, shift and
   rotation costs and satisfies $C_0 = T + N + C_{\mathrm{floor}} - \mathrm{Cov}$
   exactly. Noise amplitudes are fitted on training sessions only; a test
   session reaching the fit is an error.

### Units, Frames, and Validity

Covariances carry the squared units of their channels, and the outcome in
radians (reported in degrees). Joint channels use the joint coordinates of the
model; the closure rows use the grip frame above. A linear result is valid
only inside the nonlinearity gate, whose threshold has no default and must be
supplied by the caller. Near-grazing contact, saturation and slip need Monte
Carlo, and the linear and paired Monte Carlo values are reported together.

### Implemented and Unavailable Pieces

Strategies S1, S2, S3, S5, S7 and S8 are implemented. S4, S6, S9, S11 and S12
are not implemented and S10 is unavailable (rigid club); these are listed as
not attempted with their reason and no numbers. The only sensitivity provider is
a pendulum test fixture with invented amplitudes. No real-engine provider is
wired. The real-capture UCM and TNC report is deferred.

### Acceptance and Open Validation

Software acceptance is the NSX test suite and the golden fixtures, which show
that the code reproduces its own equations. Physical acceptance needs the five
preregistered experiments in `docs/development/planning/DV-12554.md`
(calibrated face and launch measurement, instrumented grip, perturbation-derived
impedance, EMG co-contraction ratios, randomized strategy interventions). None
has been run. Every claim type is blocked or deferred in
`docs/research/loop_nullspace/publication_gate.md`.

### Limitations and Non-Claims

Noise amplitudes, impedance and delay are declared hypotheses, not measurements.
The model is first order about the nominal swing and uses a rigid club. No
claim that any golfer uses a minimum-variance allocation, that a modelled
dispersion is a measured one, or that any strategy ranking is a coaching
prescription. No stiffness, co-contraction or muscle force is inferred from net
joint torques. EMG is an activation proxy only.

## Unavailable Values

Any quantity whose validity gate fails, whose direction is unbounded, or whose
solver backend is missing is reported `UNAVAILABLE` with a reason. It is never
reported as zero or as a large number.

## Non-Claims

No numerical result about any golfer. No claim that any single hand split is
the golfer's. No stiffness or co-contraction inference from net joint torques.
